grader_notes: The agent correctly processed metabolomics data and performed differential abundance analysis with multiple testing correction. However, the spiker classification method deviated from the required median-split approach, and the absence of phenotype correlation analysis prevents completion of the mediating lipid analysis. The biological interpretation is limited.

criterion_1.reason: Spiker classification used a within-subject comparison (potato > grape) instead of independent median splits per food, so subjects are forced into one group rather than allowing independent classifications.

criterion_2.reason: Metabolomics data was aggregated by subject-level means, log2-transformed, and differential abundance tested via linear model with log2FC and raw p-values reported.

criterion_3.reason: Top 10 metabolites ranked by raw p-value; lipid species identified with names and classes (TUDCA, LPCs); direction and fold change provided.

criterion_4.reason: No correlation analysis between top-10 lipids and the four metabolic phenotypes (SSPG, Hepatic IR, DI, IE) was performed.

criterion_5.reason: Mediating lipids were not identified because phenotype correlation was omitted; no integration of differential abundance with correlation criteria was attempted.

criterion_6.reason: OLS on log-transformed data is appropriate; BH-FDR correction applied across all metabolites with both raw and adjusted p-values reported; top-10 selection based on raw p.

criterion_7.reason: Results presented with statistics table, but biological interpretation remains generic amino-acid/phospholipid comments without specific mechanistic linkage to insulin resistance or beta-cell function.

criterion_8.reason: Numerical results are traceable to data files and lipid identifiers from data; biological interpretation lacks citations to real references, but no hallucinated claims.
